'''Ayabadhu''' (''Ayapathu''), or '''Badhu''', is an [[Language extinction|extinct]] [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] of the [[Paman languages|Paman family]] spoken on the [[Cape York Peninsula]] of [[North Queensland]], [[Australia]] by the [[Ayapathu|Ayapathu people]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /><ref name="verstraete2015">{{cite book |last1=Verstraete |first1=Jean-Christophe |last2=Rigsby |first2=Bruce |title=A Grammar and Lexicon of Yintyingka |publisher=Walter de Gruyter |year=2015 |doi=10.1515/9781614519003 |isbn=978-1-5015-0071-8 |url=https://doi.org/10.1515/9781614519003}}</ref>{{rp|17}} The Ayabadhu language region includes the [[Shire of Cook|Cook Shire]] and the areas around [[Coen, Queensland|Coen]] and [[Port Stewart, Queensland|Port Stewart]].<ref name=":SLQ44">{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/ayabadhu-44?embed=true|title=Ayabadhu|publisher=[[State Library of Queensland]]|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|url-status=live|accessdate=3 June 2022}}</ref>

Verstraete and Rigsby (2015) determined that Ayabadhu and Yintyingka, spoken by the [[Yintyingka]] and [[Lama Lama people|Lamalama]] and previously known as coastal Ayapathu, are closely related and dialects of the same language.<ref name="verstraete2015" />{{rp|51}} They also found these dialects to be "structurally different" to [[Pakanha language|Western Ayapathu]].<ref name="austlangY236">{{cite web |title=Y236: Yintyingka |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y236 |access-date=3 June 2022 |website=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |date=26 July 2019 |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]]}}</ref> The name ''Yintjinggu''/''Jintjingga'' has been used for both Ayabadhu and the neighboring [[Umbindhamu language]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /><ref name="austlangY50">{{cite web |title=Y50: Umpithamu |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y50 |access-date=3 June 2022 |website=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |date=26 July 2019 |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]]}}</ref>

* Consonants may show [[gemination]] {{IPA|[Cː]}} when in intervocalic position after a stressed initial-syllable with a short vowel.
* Stops may be heard as [[voice (phonetics)|voiced]] {{IPA|[b, ɡ, d̪, ɟ, d]}} when following nasal sounds or within the onset of a third syllable in trisyllablic words.
* {{IPA|/t/}} may also have a [[trilled consonant|trilled]] allophone {{IPA|[tʳ]}} within the onset of a second syllable.
* {{IPA|/w/}} may also be heard as a fricative {{IPAblink|β}} or an approximant {{IPAblink|β̞}} within intervocalic positions.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Verstraete |first1=Jean-Christophe |title=A Grammar and Lexicon of Yintyingka |last2=Rigsby |first2=Bruce |publisher=Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton |year=2015}}</ref>

== Vocabulary ==
Some words from the Ayabadhu language, as spelt and written by Ayabadhu authors include:<ref name=":SLQ44" />

* {{lang|ayd|'Agu}}: land
* {{lang|ayd|'Eka}}: head
* {{lang|ayd|Kaleny}}: uncle
* {{lang|ayd|Kangka}}: leaf
* {{lang|ayd|Ko'on}}: magpie goose
* {{lang|ayd|Kuche}}: two
* {{lang|ayd|Mayi}}: food
* {{lang|ayd|Punga}}: sun
* {{lang|ayd|Wanthi punga}}: good day
